part.text:
Done — all 31 tests in bowling_test.py pass (`Ran 31 tests ... OK`).

**Implementation** (bowling.py only, no other files touched):

- **`roll(pins)`** — validates pins are 0–10, rejects rolls after the game is complete, and tracks game state:
  - Frames 1–9: a frame advances on a strike/spare (frame pins reach 10) or after two rolls (open frame); the two rolls in a frame can't exceed 10 pins.
  - Frame 10: tracked separately with up to 3 rolls. A strike earns two bonus rolls, a spare one; the second and third bonus rolls must respect the 10-pin limit unless the previous bonus roll was a strike. The game ends once the 10th frame's required rolls are in.
- **`score()`** — raises if the game is incomplete (fewer than 10 frames, or missing 10th-frame bonus rolls). Otherwise it scores frames 1–9 with the standard rules (strike = 10 + next two rolls, spare = 10 + next roll, open = sum) and adds the raw sum of the 10th frame's rolls.

The first version had one bug — open frames never advanced the frame counter since I only advanced on reaching 10 pins — which I fixed by counting rolls per frame.
